newsitem.title: ITALY: Iri ponders Autostrade share conversion.
newsitem.headline: Iri ponders Autostrade share conversion.

text.p: The head of Italian state industrial holding Iri said Iri must consider converting preference shares in state motorway manager Autostrade into ordinary ones for its privatisation.

Michele Tedeschi, chairman of Iri, said in a speech to a lower house environment committee that 10 to 15 percent of Autostrade capital should be reserved for a stable core of shareholders in the process of privatising the company.
"The current structure of Autostrade means we must consider whether to convert preference shares into ordinary ones," he said.
Tedeschi also said: "I think the stake which should be reserved for a stable set of shareholders should not be less than 10 to 15 percent of the share capital."
"The level of investors' individual stakes should be between 0.5 and five percent of capital," he said.
"The stable nucleus of investors should be made up principally of institutional and financial investors," he said.

Tedeschi confirmed the objective was to privatise Autostrade by June. He said the stable shareholder structure was due to be completed in May and that such an agreement "will have to include a premium in respect to the price offered to other investors."
He said all Iri's steps to prepare the sell-off were in an advance stage.
